text:
maria: Quick thought  we need a lightweight preflight for new model intake to avoid wasting long benches. call it "rapid-ingest": binary sanity -> tiny format smoke -> micro-perf probe -> staircase warmup. aim for fast-fail on obvious issues.

alex: Yep. So the micro-probe is important. I suggest micro-probe = 8 varied inputs, seq len 32/128 mix, batch=1-2. If its way off baseline we mark slowpath.

jin: Agreed. Let's pick conservative thresholds so we don't surface false positives. Something like: fail if token/s < 0.6 * family_baseline OR p95 > 3x baseline. Also emit an anomaly flag for decode-length mismatches or control tokens in outputs.

sam: Add an explicit quantization/ops compatibility gate before any GPU runs. Cheap converter validation + op profile + memory estimate on CPU. If converter fails -> immediate reject with logs.

opsbot: converter-check: ~20-35s on small instance. cpu-forward-smoke: ~8-15s depending on model.

benchbot: micro-probe median numbers were seeing for xx-family: token/s=2800 (short), p95=12ms; for yy-family token/s=900, p95=38ms.

alex: Good. For warmup I like a staircase (progressive) approach rather than full blast. Example policy below.

```yaml
warmup_policy:
  mode: staircase  # quick | staircase | full
  steps_sequence: [50, 200, 800]
  eval_after_each: true
  pass_criteria: "p95 < 1.6x baseline AND kv_fill_delta > 7%"
  max_gpu_minutes: 40
```

jin: Staircase is safer. After each stage we compute kv_fill_delta, latency delta, and decide to continue. Also capture warmup_wear_in (how many tokens contributed to kv usefulness).

maria: What metrics must the prober emit so rollout automation can decide?

sam: Minimal required metrics: ["micro_tokens_per_sec","micro_latency_p95","kv_fill_ratio","kv_fill_delta","warmup_steps_total","warmup_gpu_minutes","binary_check_status","decode_length_mismatch_count"]. Also attach sample outputs for the micro-probe and converter logs.

alex: Operational flow for failures: if binary_check fails -> model rejected with converter logs. If micro-probe fails but binary_check passed -> move to slowpath review queue (human), attach micro-probe snapshot + quick traces. Allow optional re-run with alternate seed/sample.

maria: For audit we should snapshot the deterministic sample + seed and store it in model metadata. That makes slowpath investigations reproducible.

benchbot: Suggested diagnostic bundle size: ~3MB: micro-probe outputs, 1-2 traces, converter profile.

opsbot: Also compute a cost_estimate field for the intake UI using warmup_policy and family baseline. This helps sales/ops predict reserved capacity. Example: cost_estimate.gpu_minutes = sum(steps_sequence) * family_factor / concurrency.

ajin: Small note: name mismatch between teams: some call this "scanback"; others "rapid-ingest". Let's standardize on "rapid-ingest" in RFC, mention alias.

alex: One more: make warmup_policy configurable per-catalog model entry. Some families (decoder-only, large context) need longer first-stage warmups.

maria: Decision summary: 1) implement rapid-ingest stages: binary_check, micro_probe, staircase_warmup. 2) thresholds: token/s < 0.6*baseline OR p95 > 3x baseline -> slowpath. 3) binary_check failure -> reject w/ logs. 4) micro-probe logs + deterministic snapshot attached to metadata. 5) warmup_policy pluggable per-family + cost_estimate computed for UI. I'll write RFC with flow diagram, config schema, and metric contract. Can everyone review tomorrow morning?

jin: I'll review.

sam: count me in.

alex: Same, I'll add family baseline numbers and quick examples.

benchbot: FYI: if you want rough numbers for cost_estimate, ping me with family names and concurrency assumptions.

maria: thanks all. I'll drop a draft RFC in #eng-ml-rfcs by EOD.
